questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English as the spoken langauage, student life in the city, the weather, the culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistence regarding the choice of courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The host institution provided a link to a recommended student housing (Scape) and from here, you can see the available types of housing and the price. It was very easy and I could even request to stay in the same apartment as a friend from Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, even compared to Copenhagen. Those who chose to find housing on their own had a harder time finding a room, but was a lot cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were to choose our prefered courses ("units of study") and timetables for lectures and tutoring classes (øvelseshold). During the first week, we could attend our original chosen units of study and decide if we wanted to change them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The host institution held Enrolment Advising sessions, and the host institution also provided detailed descriptions on the processes through e-mail, which were very easy to follow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got to take all of the classes I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend the Enrolment Advising sessions at campus, and ask all the questions you might have.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses were a little below the level at UCPH. I took classes of first and second year BA which allowed me to spend my free time exploring the culture and socialise.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My host country was still affected by Covid which meant that a lot of the teaching was online. The passion in the teaching at the host institution was much higher than that of UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Race, Diversity, Difference	
Learning in Outdoor Education
Sociology of Terror
Introduction to Crime and Criminology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Terror was very interesting! However, also intense content. 
Learning in outdoor education was a lot of fun and very related to my exchange destination.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of activities; food related ones, animal-related, all sorts of sports and cultural activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The food walking tour in the introduction week. I went by myself, as most others did, and met so many cool people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible! If you plan your timetable well (you can choose among several), you can have plenty of long weekends to do smaller trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I cannot think of any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open-mindedness, laid back lifestyle, appreciation of and care for nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There are many interesting courses, try to attend many in the first week and decide as you go along. The decision could very well be based on exams too; I chose courses which ended early in the semester, meaning I had a lot of time to travel and explore my destination. 
It will be a very expensive experience, but it will be so worth it. 

If possible, try to arrange housing on your own. This will save you a lot of money that can be spent on adventures instead.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university holds enrolment weeks with lots of activities and opportunities to meet other students. I met so many new friends through these.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I found a very nice balance between studying and free time; this was definitely both due to the interesting courses, and my priority of exploring new places with new friends as often as possible.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My experience was that it was very far from home for many people. I did not mind it but I met other Danes who found it very hard.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
